coverage.summary: Applies to Philadelphia residential rentals, as invoked by tenant classes against landlords. The only source, a secondary one, states no building-type, unit-count, construction-date or landlord-size limits for Phila. Code § 9-813.

evidence.quoted_span: a class of Philadelphia tenants allege that Willow Bridge subscribed to and used RealPage services in violation of Philadelphia Code § 9-813
Philadelphia’s ordinance permits an aggrieved person to elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, together with equitable relief, interest and attorney fees and costs.

result.notes: DX06 is a secondary law-firm alert and does not reproduce the ordinance's coverage provisions. All coverage limits are therefore null. requires_unknown_facts is set to false because nothing in the source limits the ordinance to a class of buildings that assessor data cannot identify, such as subsidized units; it reads as a general restriction on landlords' use of algorithmic rent coordination. This should be checked against the official text of Phila. Code § 9-813, including any unit-count or landlord-size thresholds (compare Portland's 16-unit threshold, which the same alert mentions) and any exemptions. The original summary described the absence of coverage limits, which cannot be supported by a verbatim quote, so it was rewritten to rest on the source's description of tenant claims.
